messages.subject: Generate report only based on physical activity and not involving sleep detection
parts:
Dear Vincent,

I would like to investigate how accurate the actigraphy device register movements. I want to evaluate the registration of movements without performing sleep detection algorithms. I would like to generate a visual report with information about the physical activity during the wear time without the inclusion of information about the sleep classification. I don't want to apply the sleep scoring methods when generating the results about physical activity. I changed mode = c(1,2,3,4,5) into mode=c(1,2) or mode=(1,2,3) and do.report = c(2,4,5) at the end of the script into do.report=c(2). I am not sure if i need to  include part 3 when I don't want to analyze anything about sleep, but only analyze physical activity. Can you help me with generating visual reports with information about the physical activity without applying the sleep scoring methods?

Kind regards, 

Carlijn

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Generate report only based on physical activity and not involving sleep detection
parts:
Hi Carlijn,

Here some answers to your questions:

1. I would like to generate the acceleration in the x-, y- and z-direction. Like the picture I added.
Can you help me explaining how to achieve this?
How can I generate a visualization of these signals?
A bin file is generated as output of every part. I had not managed to read the binfile into python yet, because of its size. But maybe this will give the result I need. What would you recommend?

GGIR does not provide visualizations as the ones you share. The main functionalities of GGIR are related to data processing and extracting meaningful variables related to physical activity, sleep and circadian rhythms from the accelerometer raw signal. Some visualizations are also generated in GGIR, but only as supporting output information, so they are mostly hardcoded and there is not much the user can do to change these visualizations. In your picture attached it seems that the accelerometer raw signal for each axis is plotted, you might just need to read your accelerometer file and try to draw a plot from that data.

2. The graph in the report with the classification of 'light', 'moderate', 'vigorous', 'non-wear' of activity, is also interesting. To achieve this report including this graph the sleep classification steps are taken. This will give me additional information.

I guess you refer to the plot in the folder "results/file summary reports/". These visualizations contains a couple of acceleration metrics calculated in GGIR (not the raw signal as you showed inyour picture), and an approximation to the behavioral classification that is made in GGIR (including the physical activity intensities among other variables). And yes, to get these plots, you need to run all the parts in GGIR, including the sleep detection.

3. In the output folder - meta - sleep.qc that is generated by running the file, there is a document called 'graphyperday_id...' generated. A grey, a yellow, a red, a blue and a black line are illustrated. What does each line mean? Maybe this figure could be of added value to describe the acceleration in each direction.

The colored horizontal lines are the sustained inactivity bouts identified in g.part3, you might want to look at the main vignette with information on GGIR, its purpose and main functionalities.

Hope this answer clarify some of your questions.

Best,
Jairo
